assumptions.text: On a Screening Service outage (ScreeningService.screen raising ScreeningUnavailableError), the quote must be refused with status "refused_screening", the stored quote updated to that status, no price computed, and a refusal notice sent, following notes/analysis_notes.md as the resolution of REQ-06/OD-1.
If ScreeningService.screen raises ScreeningUnavailableError after the draft is stored, the response must still include quote_id (since a draft exists) but never include price.

If QuoteStore.update_quote fails (raises StoreUnavailableError) after the draft is stored, this is treated as an unhandled error; the behavior is not specified, so the implementation allows the exception to propagate rather than mapping it to a CargoQuote status.
If TariffEngine.price raises an unexpected exception, behavior is unspecified in the docs; the implementation lets the exception propagate instead of mapping it to a defined status.

If NotificationService methods raise exceptions (delivery failure or other), they are swallowed so that the outcome and response remain unchanged, in line with the fire-and-forget rule and REQ-07, even though the precise exception signaling mechanism is not defined.

claims.text: Validation (DT-V) is performed first; any violation yields status "rejected: invalid_request" and stops all further processing (no draft stored, no screening, no pricing, no notification).
On storage failure when storing the draft quote, status must be "error: store_unavailable" and nothing else runs (no screening, pricing, or notification).

After a valid request is stored as a draft, the Screening Service is called to obtain an integer risk_index for the shipper, and DT-S is applied to determine the outcome band (accept, review, refuse).
For accept-band risk_index (risk_index <= 41), the status is "quoted", the quote is priced per DT-P, stored, and a quote document is sent.
For review-band risk_index (42 <= risk_index <= 66), the status is "review_hold", the quote is stored, and there is no price computation and no notification.
For refuse-band risk_index (risk_index >= 67), the status is "refused_screening", the quote is stored, no price is computed, and a refusal notice is sent.
Notification is fire-and-forget; a delivery failure never changes the stored quote or the response.

Pricing DT-P rules: base = 0.87 * weight_kg + 1.13 * distance_km; if weight_kg > 1244 add 316.00; if distance_km >= 4912 multiply the running total by 1.19 after the heavy surcharge step; final price is round(result, 2).
The API response must always contain a status, include quote_id whenever a draft was stored, and include price only on priced rows (accept-band).
The overall flow order is: validate → store draft → screening → apply DT-S and update stored quote status → pricing (if priced) → notification (if notified) → return response.
